issues.failure_explanation: Testing (relativeporo2) with v_r gives RHS (2\rho_f\phi\ff_P, v_r), but F contains (\rho_f\phi\ff_P, v_r) (factor 2 missing). Testing (relativeporo1) with w_s gives RHS ((\rho_p+\rho_f\phi)\ff_P, w_s), but F contains (\rho_p\ff_P, w_s) (the \rho_f\phi\ff_P term missing). Additionally, r_S appears in F and in the stability estimate but is never defined; the continuity equation (stokes2) has zero source, so r_S should be 0.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the source terms in F to match the PDE (add factor 2 to the v_r term and \rho_f\phi\ff_P to the w_s term, or remove the corresponding terms from the PDE) and set r_S = 0 or define it consistently with the continuity equation. Re-derive F from the tested PDEs to ensure consistency.
issues.overall_effect: The weak formulation \eqref{n_weak} does not represent the stated PDE system. All discrete schemes and analysis results are established for a different right-hand side than the model equations specify. The numerical convergence tests cannot validate the PDE as written.
issues.title: Weak-form source functional F inconsistent with PDE; r_S undefined
issues.why_classification: Multiple source-term corrections and an undefined variable require re-deriving F and deciding whether the PDE or F is authoritative. The analysis structure survives but the mathematical content changes depending on the chosen repair.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof bounds only the diagonal blocks of A (the a_f^S, a_f^P, a_s^P terms on each velocity component separately) and concludes A is coercive. The block operator A contains significant off-diagonal coupling terms (BJS cross-terms a_{BJS}(u_f,y_s;v_f,w_s), interface terms N_{sf,\Gamma}, B_{e,\Gamma}, mass-matrix cross terms M_{\rho_f\phi}), none of which are shown to be absorbed by the diagonal coercivity. Bounding diagonal blocks individually does not establish coercivity of the full block operator.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Show that all off-diagonal coupling terms in the block operator A can be bounded via Young's inequality and absorbed by the diagonal coercivity bounds (from Korn's and trace inequalities), yielding coercivity of A on the full product space with a quantified coercivity constant.
issues.overall_effect: The ellipticity of A (and hence ker(A) = {0}) is unproved, invalidating the kernel condition in Lemma \ref{invertibilty}, the invertibility argument for M+N, and all well-posedness, stability, and error results downstream.
issues.title: Coercivity of block operator A not established (off-diagonal coupling unaccounted)
issues.why_classification: A contained absorption argument for the cross terms should suffice without new global proof architecture, but it requires a nontrivial estimate that is absent.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma \ref{usual_inf} gives an inf-sup constant \xi_1 for the sup over the full space V_h. The proof of Lemma \ref{inf_sup} restricts the supremum to the proper subspace V_{h,0} (which imposes the strong mass-balance constraint on normal traces at \Sigma) and claims the same constant \xi_1 applies. An inf-sup condition on a subspace is not inherited from the full space; the constraint can destroy the lower bound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove the inf-sup condition on V_{h,0} by a separate argument (e.g., a lifting or decomposition constructing velocity fields satisfying the normal-trace constraint while maintaining the divergence pairing), or restructure the proof to avoid restricting to V_{h,0}.
issues.overall_effect: The discrete inf-sup condition for the Nitsche-augmented B block is unproved, invalidating ker(\phi_{B^T}) = {0} in Lemma \ref{invertibilty} and the invertibility and well-posedness results downstream.
issues.title: Inf-sup constant from full space incorrectly applied to constrained subspace V_{h,0}
issues.why_classification: Proving inf-sup on the constrained subspace requires a nontrivial new argument (decomposition or lifting), but it is a contained lemma that preserves the overall well-posedness architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma \ref{invertibilty1} asserts that positive semi-definiteness of A and C together with the kernel conditions implies invertibility of M+N in generalized saddle-point form [[A, B^T], [-B, C]]. No proof or citation is provided. While the result is a standard saddle-point invertibility criterion, the argument (kernel of the block matrix is trivial via PSD and kernel-intersection conditions) is nontrivial and absent from the source.

failure_location.quote: then the matrix $\mathbf{M} + \mathbf{N}$ is invertible for any given $ \bw_{f,h}^{\mathrm{S}} \in \mathbf{K}_h$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Supply the standard proof: for the homogeneous system [[A, B^T],[-B, C]][u;p]=0, multiply by (u^T, p^T), use PSD of A and C to get u in ker(A) and p in ker(C), then use the two kernel-intersection conditions to conclude u = p = 0; square matrix with trivial kernel is invertible.
issues.overall_effect: The nonsingularity of M+N (needed for DAE existence and fully discrete solvability) is asserted without justification.
issues.title: Invertibility lemma for M+N stated without proof
issues.why_classification: The proof is short and standard (5-6 lines using PSD and kernel arguments); providing it is a routine addition that preserves every claim.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: are consistent and do not lead to any incompatibility issues.

issues.failure_explanation: The mass matrix M in the DAE system M \partial_t x + N x = L has a zero sixth column (the variable u_s has no time derivative in any equation), so M is singular and the system does have an algebraic constraint (u_s = \partial_t y_s from the fourth equation). Having no zero rows does not imply absence of algebraic constraints. For a DAE with singular mass matrix, the initial data must satisfy compatibility conditions (here u_{s,0} = \partial_t y_s(0)), which are merely asserted ('consistent and do not lead to any incompatibility issues') without verification.

failure_location.quote: The matrix \(E\) has no zero rows, which implies that the system has no algebraic constraints.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Eliminate u_s using the algebraic constraint u_s = \partial_t y_s to obtain a reduced DAE with a nonsingular mass matrix (avoiding the consistency issue), or explicitly verify u_{s,0} = \partial_t y_s(0) and apply DAE theory with the correct constraint structure.
issues.overall_effect: Existence of a semi-discrete solution is not established as claimed; the DAE theory result requires verified initial-data consistency which is absent.
issues.title: DAE analysis incorrectly claims absence of algebraic constraints; consistency of initial data unverified
issues.why_classification: The fix requires reformulating the DAE or verifying compatibility, which is a contained but nontrivial argument change; the well-posedness conclusion survives in the reduced system.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we employ Banach's fixed-point theorem by demonstrating that the operator $\mathcal{J}_h$ admits a unique fixed point in the set $\mathbf{K}_h$.

issues.failure_explanation: Banach's fixed-point theorem requires J_h to map K_h into itself (self-mapping) and to be a contraction. The proof establishes only the contraction property (the Lipschitz bound \|J_h(w_1) - J_h(w_2)\| \leq (1/3)\|w_1 - w_2\|). The self-mapping property J_h(K_h) \subset K_h, i.e., \|\nabla J_h(w)\|_0 \leq (1/(CS_f^2K_f^3))\|f_S\|_0 for w \in K_h, is never proved. Without self-mapping, the fixed-point theorem does not apply.

failure_location.quote: In turn, these steps establish that $\mathcal{J}_h$ is a contraction mapping.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Derive a stability estimate for the linearized Oseen/poroelasticity problem showing \|u_f\|_{1,\Omega_S} \leq (1/(CS_f^2K_f^3))\|f_S\|_0 for the first component u_f = J_h(w) of the solution, thereby establishing J_h(K_h) \subset K_h.
issues.overall_effect: Well-posedness of the semi-discrete Nitsche scheme (existence of a fixed point of J_h) is not established, so the main well-posedness claim of Theorem \ref{thm:added-1} is unsupported.
issues.title: Banach fixed-point argument proves contraction but not self-mapping of K_h
issues.why_classification: Establishing self-mapping requires a contained energy estimate (standard for Oseen-type problems) but is a nontrivial missing step; the contraction argument and overall architecture survive.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof claims that L = (1/\tau)M + N has 'the same structure' as M+N and is therefore nonsingular. Having the same block structure does not imply nonsingularity: scaling M by 1/\tau changes the matrix entries (e.g., the (4,3) entry becomes M_{-\rho_p}/\tau instead of M_{-\rho_p}), which can alter the kernel. Additionally, the conclusion references \eqref{mixed-primal} instead of \eqref{discrete_matrix}.

failure_location.quote: This resulting matrix has the same structure as $\mathbf{M} + \mathbf{N}$, which is shown to be nonsingular in the proof of Lemma~\ref{invertibilty}. Therefore, the scaled matrix is nonsingular, and so is the matrix in \eqref{mixed-primal}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove that (1/\tau)M + N is nonsingular directly, e.g., by showing the kernel conditions (ker(A_\tau) \cap ker(B) = {0} and ker(C_\tau) \cap ker(B^T) = {0}) hold for the scaled block matrices, or by a coercivity argument on the full scaled system.
issues.overall_effect: Unique solvability of the fully discrete algebraic system is not established, so the stability lemma and error estimates (which assume a unique solution exists) are unreliable.
issues.title: Fully discrete solvability argument invalid (structure preservation does not imply nonsingularity)
issues.why_classification: A kernel or coercivity argument for the scaled matrix is a contained proof addition, but the existing reasoning ('same structure implies nonsingular') is invalid and must be replaced.

issues.failure_explanation: The projection \Pi_{r,h} is specified by the divergence-preserving property (mfe1) and an L^2 approximation bound (mfe3) of order h^{r_{kp}-1}. However, the error estimate for u_r has rate h^{2r_{kp}-2} = (h^{r_{kp}-1})^2, which requires an H^1 approximation bound \|u_r - \Pi_{r,h} u_r\|_1 \leq Ch^{r_{kp}-1}\|u_r\|_{H^{r_{kp}}}. This H^1 property is neither stated in (mfe1)-(mfe3) nor derived; the projection is under-specified and the needed bound is not guaranteed by the given properties alone.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State and prove (or cite from a standard reference) the H^1 approximation property of \Pi_{r,h}: \|v - \Pi_{r,h}v\|_1 \leq Ch^{r_{kp}-1}\|v\|_{H^{r_{kp}}}, and include it alongside (mfe1)-(mfe3) as a stated property of the projection.
issues.overall_effect: The convergence rate for the relative-velocity error is unsupported as stated; the error estimate in Theorem \ref{appendix_fully} relies on an approximation property not established in the source.
issues.title: Error analysis uses H^1 approximation of Stokes projection \Pi_{r,h} not stated in its properties
issues.why_classification: The missing property is standard for the intended projection but requires a nontrivial interpolation estimate to establish; the analysis architecture and claimed rates survive once the property is supplied.

issues.failure_explanation: In the decomposition of the nonlinear convective error J_9, the term u_f^{S,n-1} \cdot \nabla(\chi_f^n + \phi_f^n) involves the exact solution u_f^{S,n-1}. The subsequent bound derives (\mu_f/2)\|\nabla\phi_f^n\|_0^2 from this term using the small-data assumption \|u_{f,h}^{S,n}\|_1 < \mu_f/(2S_f^2K_f^3), which bounds the discrete solution at time n, not the exact solution at time n-1. The L^4 norm of the exact solution u_f^{S,n-1} is not controlled by the small-data assumption on u_{f,h}^{S,n}, so the inference is invalid.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Split u_f^{S,n-1} = u_{f,h}^{S,n-1} + \chi_f^{n-1} + \phi_f^{n-1} in the nonlinear decomposition: bound the discrete part using the small-data assumption on u_{f,h}^{S,n-1} and the error part using approximation and error norms, absorbing the resulting terms via Young's inequality and discrete Gronwall.
issues.overall_effect: The bound on the nonlinear error term J_9 is unsupported, so the overall error estimate in Theorem \ref{appendix_fully} is not established.
issues.title: Nonlinear error bound uses small-data assumption on discrete velocity to bound exact-solution term
issues.why_classification: The fix requires a contained but nontrivial splitting argument with additional error terms absorbed by Gronwall; the error estimate structure and claimed rates survive.
